candidates.term: The Sage at the Month Gate
candidates.defline: The Sage stands at your Month Gate, in plain view: at work you are seen as the calm one who knows things.
candidates.reading: Your working years have been shaped by how credible you look, the person with the knowledge and the steady manner. Because older colleagues trust you early, they open doors for you, and your career moves through reputation and study more than through pushing. Colleagues and friends bring you their problems for the same reason. You give a great deal of calm away, and you are rarely the one anyone thinks to look after.
candidates.teaser: The working world reads you as credible: the one with the knowledge and the calm. Your career advances through reputation and study, and elders open the doors.

domain_readings.Career: The working world reads you as credible: the one with the knowledge and the calm, promoted through reputation and study rather than push. Elders open your doors. Keep learning in public. Every course and kindness compounds into the name that becomes your salary’s engine.
domain_readings.Mind: Your mind advances by absorption: study that becomes instinct, knowledge worn so naturally it reads as temperament. You learn continuously and forget to claim it. Claim it. Credentials are your native currency, and the mint is always open.
domain_readings.Social: You become the counselor early: the colleague consulted, the friend who holds confidences, the calm one in every storm. The role deepens with rank. Set its hours. Even the counsel table needs closing time, and yours never learned one.

candidates.life_chapter: Your rising chapter earns its reputation reading: the prime decades convert study into standing, references into rank, calm into authority. Expect elders to sponsor you and juniors to consult you, often in the same season. The era trusts you early. Deserve it on schedule.
candidates.relations: The door-opening elders are this seat’s people: mentors who sponsored, seniors who vouched, the lineage of teachers running through your career. You are the next link. Sponsor somebody before you feel senior enough. That is exactly when it counts.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the credential waits unfinished: learning continuous, claiming postponed. Complete one public qualification this year. The name compounds on paper.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the counselor never closes: everyone’s calm, nobody’s evening. Post the hours and keep them.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, credibility becomes caretaking: trusted by all, tended by none.
candidates.health_line: Your steadiness spends real energy: holding the calm for others draws on your reserves. Refill in solitude and study, your original medicines.

Career.headline: You rise at work because people trust you.
Career.recognition: References, qualifications and the good word of people senior to you win you roles. Because steadiness is what you offer, you are given responsibility early, and you rarely have to sell yourself. You find open competition uncomfortable and do your best work where trust is already in place.
Career.lived: Since your late teens older people at work have backed you, vouched for you or quietly put your name forward. You have collected qualifications and references in those years that still carry weight wherever you apply, and you have needed to push less than most.

Mind.headline: Knowledge becomes second nature to you.
Mind.recognition: You learn by steady absorption, and what you study becomes part of how you think without effort. Because the learning feels natural to you, you forget how much of it you have, and others notice before you do. You underrate your own knowledge more than anyone around you does.
Mind.lived: From your late teens you took in courses, books and advice from people who knew more, and kept nearly all of it. Over those years you came to know your field better than you let on, and you have rarely made a show of it.

Social.headline: Your friends bring you their troubles.
Social.recognition: You become the friend people confide in, the calm one who listens and gives sound advice. Because being trusted feels like a kind of care to you, you rarely say no, and your evenings fill with other people's problems. You find it hard to ask for the same help yourself.
Social.lived: Since your late teens you have been the one friends and colleagues come to when something goes wrong. You have kept more confidences than you can count, and few people have asked how you were doing in return.
